newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone to take extra albumin charges. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Rhone to take extra albumin charges. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Finance Director Jean-Pierre Tirouflet said on Friday the company would take total charges for the voluntary recall of albumin products of between 100 million and 200 million francs at the net level for 1996.
This includes the 81 million franc charge taken in the third quarter.
"The provision will be between 100 and 200 million francs," he told a news conference.
Tirouflet reaffirmed the total effect on net profits of the recall by the Centeon joint venture with Hoechst would reduce 1996 net income by six to seven percent compared to analysts forecasts.

Asked to comment on a forecast of 2.75 billion (corrects from 2.5 billion) francs for the 1996 net profits, Tirouflet said, "I have lower (analysts) forecasts in my head." Rhone-Poulenc later clarified that Tirouflet was not making an official company forecast.
(Corrects reference figure and makes clear Tirouflet was not giving a company forecast)
He said the group's asset sale programme would stand at between seven to nine billion francs at the end of the year.
Rhone-Poulenc had set itself an aim of selling 10 billion francs in non-strategic assets before the end of 1997 and had sold six billion francs on September 30, 1996.
He declined to give a specific profit forecast for 1996 but said 1996 net profit would be higher than 1995.
At the nine-month stage net income was already up 10.5 percent compared to the first nine months of 1995 at 2.17 billion francs,

Tirouflet said the pharmaceuticals sector would see further growth in the fourth quarter as the synergy effects of the Fisons merger would come to cruising speed and due to the effect of the launch of new products.
In chemicals, fourth quarter income would be less than that of the third quarter, but better than the fourth quarter 1995.
Tirouflet also said the company would take some additional charges for restructuring in the chemicals sector. The company has already made some 200 million francs in provisions for restructuring.
Tirouflet said that there was still no signs of improvement in the chemical sector and that intermediary prices had been flat since the fourth quarter of 1995.
But he noted that chemical analysts were now expecting the top of the cycle in 1999 instead of 1998 due to economic growth in the United States.
In the agro sector Tirouflet said the fourth quarter would not be good because of seasonal factors.
